clue.text: At one time used offensively to ignore a young woman

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them
lass is a word for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Someone once insulted a girl by snubbing her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used offensively' sounds like insulting language, but the definition means a weapon wielded in attack in former times.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's short curved sword was a weapon of earlier centuries, used to attack.

clue.text: Rendered sterile, cold, and bent

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
something that has bent over has leaned

explanation.surface: Something made sterile, chilled and twisted out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing something thoroughly removes germs and dirt, making it sterile.

clue.text: A meeting of Continental heads

parts.note: a summit of European leaders, or literally French heads (the word for head in French) placed together

explanation.surface: A summit of European leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' points to French, in which the word for head appears twice in the answer, linked by the French for 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A private conversation between two people, literally 'head to head' in French.

clue.text: Encourages a sailing man set to change course,

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: changing course means the letters of the word set take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sailor is spurred on to alter his heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change course' rearranges SET into ETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To support or incite someone, usually in wrongdoing, is to encourage them.

clue.text: Transport and plant, all around small lake

indicators.note: the plant word goes completely around the letter for lake

parts.note: sedge is a grassy marsh plant
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Vehicle and vegetation encircle a little pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled pulled over snow or ice is a means of conveyance.

clue.text: For many a fool in love it's just a game

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
an ass is a foolish person
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: To a lovesick fool, romance is merely a pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: The card game is also spelt with one S; this spelling has two.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game for two to four players in which cards are captured from a layout.

clue.text: A memorial that's maybe not cheap

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of not and cheap could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A monument that probably cost a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges NOT CHEAP into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument to the war dead, especially one honouring those buried elsewhere, like the one in Whitehall.

clue.text: Fruit and fish taken on board

parts.note: a shad is a fish of the herring family
a ship docks when it comes into berth, where cargo is taken on board

explanation.surface: Fruit and fish loaded onto a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part is loose: ships load at docks, so 'taken on board' hints at the quayside where loading happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A large citrus fruit, the pomelo, ancestor of the grapefruit.

clue.text: She's always in out-moded attire, never the latest style

indicators.note: the woman's name sits inside the words that follow, across the comma

explanation.surface: A woman who always dresses in old-fashioned clothes and never follows fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so a 'she'.

clue.text: Not so smart — but so different when accompanying the queen

indicators.note: a different arrangement of the letters in but and so

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Less clever, yet otherwise when in the royal company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges BUT SO into OBTUS; 'accompanying' puts the queen's ER alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word meaning dull-witted or slow on the uptake.

clue.text: Out-and-out maximum

explanation.surface: A total, utter peak.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means complete or utter, and also of the greatest possible degree.

clue.text: Dine in a cosy home that's most elegant

indicators.note: in places the eating word inside the word for a snug home

parts.note: a nest is a snug home
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Eating at a snug home with the smartest style.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means smart and trim, so the superlative is the trimmest or most stylish.

clue.text: Widespread complaint ends as the singer breaks down

indicators.note: something that breaks down falls apart, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A common illness ends when the vocalist collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks down' rearranges ENDS AS THE SINGER into the answer; the singer collapsing is the surface story.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia, being unable to see distant things clearly, is a very common eye condition.

clue.text: Some schoolchildren choose to get wet

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few pupils decide they want to be soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak something thoroughly is to make it wet through.

clue.text: Painter set against firm

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
stable means firm or steady

explanation.surface: An artist is pitted against a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a business; it is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was an English landscape artist, painter of The Hay Wain.

clue.text: Room where drinks are dispensed for the typist?

parts.note: room in the sense of space, as in room to move
a bar is a counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: A lounge with a drinks counter, set aside for the secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as indirect: the long key at the bottom of a keyboard is something for the typist.
explanation.definitionFit: The long key on a keyboard that a typist presses between words.

clue.text: This writer backed all alternatives

indicators.note: alternatives are other versions, so the letters of backed and all take another order

explanation.surface: The author supported every option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' would usually mean the setter; here it is a writing tool, graphite.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphite, the material in pencils, is what does the writing.

clue.text: Shut up about money required for a bit of building

indicators.note: the word for confined goes about the coin word

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut up or confined
a dime is an American ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: Imprisoned over cash needed for construction work.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangular gable above a classical portico is an architectural feature.

clue.text: Jersey is of course one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Jersey is naturally counted among the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' looks like the island, but here it is a knitted sweater; the other definition is the island next door.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick knitted woollen sweater takes its name from the island, which neighbours Jersey off the French coast.

clue.text: Less experienced, perhaps, but more concerned for the environment

explanation.surface: Newer to the job but more ecologically minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means naive or new, and also environmentally aware; the comparative serves both.

clue.text: Makes an attempt at literary work

explanation.surface: Someone has a go at writing something literary.
explanation.definitionFit: To try something is a verb sense; the noun means short prose compositions, literary pieces.

clue.text: Catalogue company in some distress

parts.note: a set is a group of people, a company
to be down is to feel low or distressed

explanation.surface: A mail-order firm is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catalogue' looks like a noun for a mail-order business, but it is the verb meaning to record.
explanation.definitionFit: To write something down or record it is to list it.

clue.text: A group of managers who have got on?

parts.note: a board is the body of directors managing a company

explanation.surface: Directors who have done well in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got on' suggests success in life; the definition means having boarded a train or ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers on a ship, train or plane are on it.

clue.text: The retired may well get heated over this

definitions.text: The retired may well get heated over this

parts.words: The retired may well get heated over this
parts.note: the retired are not pensioners but people who have gone to bed, warmed by a powered cover lying over them

explanation.surface: Pensioners are likely to become angry about this matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests pensioners and 'get heated' anger; read literally, those who have retired to bed get warm under it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed cover with heating wires that warms the sleeper lying under it.

clue.text: Out of picture mounts additional supplies wanted

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-directory

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounts means the word is read climbing upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: a picture is a piece of art

explanation.surface: Frames from a picture are needed as more supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounts' looks like picture framing; in a down clue it turns ART upwards to TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more than usual or needed is additional.

clue.text: A large stretch of water, a resort for high fliers

parts.note: Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A big lake as a holiday destination for top executives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high fliers' suggests successful people; they are birds of prey, and the resort is their nest.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest, high on a crag, where the bird returns.

clue.text: Striking appears ineffective

explanation.surface: A strike seems to achieve nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words, NOT ABLE, for the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking means remarkable or noteworthy; split in two it reads 'not able', meaning incapable.

clue.text: Give the go-ahead for a welcome, nothing more

parts.note: to greet someone is to welcome them
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Approving a greeting and no more.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent to something is to approve it and let it proceed.

clue.text: Split — about time! — for scientific use

indicators.note: the word for a tear goes around the word for an era

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Breaking up at last, someone exclaims, for the benefit of science.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a substance kept for use in chemical tests.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical substance used in laboratory tests to cause or detect a reaction.

clue.text: Clothing is to be shortened before study in the big city

indicators.note: the clothing word loses its tail, cut short at the end

parts.note: dress is a word for clothing
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: Garments are to be taken up before someone studies in the metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: A large historic city in eastern Germany, capital of Saxony.
